hints: Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) to both particles: $Q$ descends vertically under gravity and tension, while $P$ moves along the smooth horizontal table under tension alone.
Set up the simultaneous equations $0.4g - T = 0.4a$ and $T = 0.6a$.
Add the equations to find the common acceleration $a$, then substitute $a$ to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Write the equation of motion for hanging particle $Q$ descending vertically:
$$0.4g - T = 0.4a \implies 4 - T = 0.4a$$

Write the equation of motion for particle $P$ on the smooth horizontal table:
$$T = 0.6a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate tension $T$ and solve for acceleration $a$:
$$4 = (0.4 + 0.6)a = 1.0a \implies a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the tension in the string:
$$T = 0.6(4) = 2.4\text{ N}$$

State the final conclusions:
$$\text{Tension } = 2.4\text{ N}, \quad \text{acceleration of } Q = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ downwards}$$
teacher_walkthrough: First, apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) to each particle connected by the light inextensible string.

For particle $Q$ of mass $m_Q = 0.4\text{ kg}$ hanging freely, the downward gravitational force is $0.4g = 0.4 \times 10 = 4\text{ N}$ and the upward tension is $T$:
$$0.4g - T = 0.4a$$
$$4 - T = 0.4a$$

For particle $P$ of mass $m_P = 0.6\text{ kg}$ on the smooth table, tension $T$ is the only horizontal force:
$$T = 0.6a$$

Substitute $T = 0.6a$ into the equation for $Q$:
$$4 - 0.6a = 0.4a$$
$$4 = 0.4a + 0.6a = 1.0a$$
$$a = \frac{4}{1.0} = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ back into the expression for $T$:
$$T = 0.6 \times 4 = 2.4\text{ N}$$

Conclude with the tension and the acceleration of $Q$:
$$\text{Tension } = 2.4\text{ N}, \quad \text{Acceleration of } Q = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ downwards}$$
